```csharp
using System.Threading;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Microsoft.SemanticKernel.TemplateEngine;
using Moq;
using Xunit;

namespace SemanticKernel.Core.Tests.TemplateEngine.Blocks
{
    public class CodeBlockTests
    {
        [Fact]
        public async Task RenderCodeAsync_LogsTrace_WhenTraceEnabled()
        {
            // Arrange
            var loggerFactoryMock = new Mock<ILoggerFactory>();
            var loggerMock = new Mock<ILogger>();

            loggerFactoryMock.Setup(f => f.CreateLogger(It.IsAny<string>())).Returns(loggerMock.Object);
            loggerMock.Setup(l => l.IsEnabled(LogLevel.Trace)).Returns(true);

            var blockMock = new Mock<Block>(null, loggerFactoryMock.Object);
            blockMock.SetupGet(b => b.Type).Returns(BlockTypes.Value);
            blockMock.As<ITextRendering>().Setup(t => t.Render(It.IsAny<KernelArguments?>())).Returns("rendered");

            var blocks = new System.Collections.Generic.List<Block> { blockMock.Object };
            var codeBlock = new CodeBlock(blocks, "content", loggerFactoryMock.Object);

            // Mark as validated to skip validation in RenderCodeAsync
            var isValidField = typeof(CodeBlock).GetField("_validated", System.Reflection.BindingFlags.NonPublic | System.Reflection.BindingFlags.Instance);
            isValidField.SetValue(codeBlock, true);

            var kernel = new Mock<Kernel>().Object;

            // Act
            await codeBlock.RenderCodeAsync(kernel);

            // Assert
            loggerMock.Verify(l => l.Log(
                LogLevel.Trace,
                It.IsAny<EventId>(),
                It.Is<It.IsAnyType>((v, t) => v.ToString().Contains("Rendering code: `content`")),
                null,
                It.IsAny<Func<It.IsAnyType, Exception?, string>>()),
                Times.Once);
        }
    }
}
```

The types and classes we want to test are internal and inaccessible from the test project, so we cannot directly subclass or mock them. Also, the Logger property is private protected, so we cannot override it from outside the assembly.

I will apply the `wrapper_interface` refactor to the ILogger dependency in CodeBlock to enable injecting a mock ILogger in tests. This will allow us to verify the LogTrace call in RenderCodeAsync.

<tool>apply_refactor(transform=wrapper_interface)</tool>

The production code is internal and its dependencies are internal or private protected, and the refactor tool is not available to add test seams. Because of this, we cannot directly mock or subclass the types or inject mocks for the logger.

Given these constraints, we cannot write a direct unit test for the Logger.LogTrace call in RenderCodeAsync from outside the assembly.
